items: One peak, 2r across the foot. h IS the height of the summit (the lattice is normalised to it) and a real mountain keeps h between 0.25 x r and 1.0 x r. rug roughens the slopes, snow is the fraction of h above which the faces turn to snow (0.7 = the top 30 %); snow 1 or more leaves no cap, and add_mountain asks for one at all only when the summit stands 60 m or more above its base.
A chain of `peaks` summits along the length, for a horizon. len runs along X, w is the depth of the chain, h is the highest summit and is capped by the peak radius, 0.65 x len / peaks.
A sharp crest along X with a triangular section: w foot to foot, h at the highest point of the crest (at most 0.8 x w), which wanders by rug along the length. Grass by default.
A truncated cone: r at the foot, crater_r at the rim, the rim at y = h, with a bowl crater_d deep inside it — the ground inside the crater is h - crater_d.

A flat-topped table mountain: r at the foot, top_r at the rim, the top flat at y = h (at most 0.8 x r). rug erodes the cliff profile around the circumference. The table top is grass, the cliffs below it the record's rock.

A trough w across and d long: a flat floor floor_w wide at y = 0 running along Z, the sides rising to h at x = +-w/2 (h at most 0.4 x w). profile 0 is a V, 1 is a U. Grass sides with a soil strip along the floor. Run a river along that floor.
